discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. show_edit_result

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. show_edit_result

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow

inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow

inspect_workflow_items

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

inspect_workflow_items

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item

focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow

If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. show_edit_result

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Thoughts:
Created the full bug-handling workflow atomically.

**Added 9 nodes**
- Input: **Report intake**
- Actions: **Triage report**, **Investigate bug**, **Fix bug**, **Request more details**
- Conditions: **Reproducible?**, **Verification passed?**
- Ends: **Release fix**, **Close incomplete**

**Added 11 connections**
- Report intake → Triage report
- Triage report (success) → Reproducible?
- Reproducible? (yes) → Investigate bug
- Reproducible? (no) → Request more details
- Investigate bug (success) → Fix bug
- Investigate bug (failure) → Close incomplete
- Fix bug (success) → Verification passed?
- Fix bug (failure) → Close incomplete
- Verification passed? (yes) → Release fix
- Verification passed? (no) → Fix bug
- Request more details (success) → Close incomplete
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Thoughts:
Created the full bug-handling workflow atomically.

**Changed:** 9 nodes and 11 connections (20 items total), including:
- Intake → triage → reproducibility decision
- Investigation and fix paths, including failure closure
- Verification loop back to fixing when verification fails
- Release on successful verification
- Incomplete closure after requesting more details
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Trajectory
Step 1
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Created the full bug-handling workflow atomically.

**Changes made**
- Added 9 nodes:
  - Input: **Report intake**
  - Actions: **Triage report**, **Investigate bug**, **Fix bug**, **Request more details**
  - Conditions: **Reproducible?**, **Verification passed?**
  - Ends: **Release fix**, **Close incomplete**
- Added 11 connections, including:
  - Reproducibility branching to investigation or more details
  - Failure paths to **Close incomplete**
  - Verification loop back to **Fix bug** when verification does not pass
  - Release path when verification passes

The resulting workflow is visible, and the edit can be undone if needed.
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 3
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.

Step 2
Available Tools (8):
discover_workflow
Call this first, once per task. Call it again only when following an itemPage or problemPage nextCursor, after a conflict, or when recovery directs you to refresh current IDs and revision. Returns a compact page of item IDs, labels, revision, valid ports, page targets, and next steps. If it answers a request to list what is on the canvas, do not call this tool again or inspect every item.
inspect_workflow_items
Call after discover_workflow only when detailed properties or relationships are requested. Returns data only; it does not select or reveal an item. For select, show, reveal, or bring into view, use show_workflow_item.
edit_workflow
Call after discover_workflow. Reuse existing IDs returned in itemPage. Before deciding an ID is absent, follow itemPage.nextCursor until it is null; one page is not proof of absence. Never create a node with an existing ID. Set baseRevision to discovery's exact revision. Do not increment it. Every command object needs a top-level type, for example {type:"createNode",node:{...}}. Never wrap a command as {createNode:{...}}. Connect with {type:"connect",edge:{id:"edge-id",source:{nodeId:"source-id",port:"success"},target:{nodeId:"target-id",port:"input"}}}. Replace with {type:"replaceConnection",edgeId:"existing-edge-id",replacements:[{...edge}]}. Other shapes are {type:"updateNode",id,patch}, {type:"deleteNode",id}, and {type:"disconnect",edgeId}. Positions and empty properties may be omitted. Applies up to 20 commands atomically and reveals the resulting receipt. When visible is true, stop; do not call get_edit_result unless the user explicitly asks for every itemized change. On conflict, rediscover before retrying.
show_workflow_item
Use this after discover_workflow whenever the user asks to select, show, reveal, or bring an item into view. Do not substitute inspect_workflow_items; inspection does not change the visible selection. For nodes, this also moves verified keyboard focus to the node.
focus_page_element
Always call discover_workflow first in the current task. Queue keyboard focus for one named page target by passing exactly one targetId value returned by discovery. The browser applies focus when the window receives focus or an accessibility interaction occurs.
get_edit_result
Retrieve paginated changes for an operationId returned by edit_workflow or undo_workflow_edit.
show_edit_result
Use after undo_workflow_edit, to revisit an existing receipt, or when edit_workflow returns visible false. Do not call it after an edit that returns visible true. Pass the operationId to bring the history entry into view and focus it as visible evidence.
undo_workflow_edit
Undo the operationId from a successful edit result when it is still the latest graph revision, then return a reversal result.
